2609.17169.title: MUMINS: Metadata-conditioned Uncertainty-aware Medical Image Next-state Synthesis
2609.17169.paper_summary: Forecasting anatomical changes such as tumor growth and neurodegeneration is a challenging generative vision task. Morphological evolution is subtle relative to static anatomy, highly patient-specific, and inherently stochastic. Existing methods struggle with several issues: deterministic networks ignore biological stochasticity, while standard diffusion models require computationally prohibitive multi-pass sampling to quantify uncertainty. We propose MUMINS (Metadata-conditioned Uncertainty-aware Medical Image Next-state Synthesis), an efficient diffusion framework that jointly diffuses a baseline scan and its follow-up residual, summed to synthesize the follow-up scan, while concurrently predicting a spatial uncertainty map, in a single reverse diffusion process. Conditioned on the time interval and relevant metadata, it preserves fine-grained anatomy by dynamically re-injecting the baseline as a soft anchor at every denoising step, and a negative-log-likelihood head learns the uncertainty map to explicitly flag error-prone regions. Designed without organ-specific heuristics, the same architecture is reused across anatomies via separate, dataset-specific retraining. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that dataset-specific retraining of MUMINS matches or outperforms dedicated, domain-specific state-of-the-art methods on lung CT (PNG) and brain MRI (OASIS-3). Project page: https://github.com/aolivtous/MUMINS.
2609.17169.paper_summary_zh: 預測解剖變化，如腫瘤生長和神經退行性變化，是一項具有挑戰性的生成視覺任務。相對於靜態解剖學，形態演變是微妙的，具有高度的個體特異性，並且本質上是隨機的。現有的方法面臨幾個問題：確定性網絡忽略了生物隨機性，而標準擴散模型則需要計算上昂貴的多次取樣來量化不確定性。我們提出了MUMINS（元數據條件的不確定性感知醫學影像下一狀態合成），這是一個高效的擴散框架，通過在單一的反向擴散過程中共同擴散基線掃描和其後續殘差，將其相加以合成後續掃描，同時預測空間不確定性圖。基於時間間隔和相關元數據進行條件處理，它通過在每個去噪步驟中動態重新注入基線作為軟錨點來保留細緻的解剖結構，並且負對數似然頭學習不確定性圖，以明確標記易出錯的區域。該架構設計不依賴於器官特定的啟發式方法，通過分開的數據集特定再訓練在不同解剖中重用相同的架構。廣泛的評估顯示，MUMINS的數據集特定再訓練在肺CT（PNG）和腦MRI（OASIS-3）上與專門的領域特定最先進方法相匹配或超越。項目頁面：https://github.com/aolivtous/MUMINS。
